question: Which public Task Session lifecycle contract should govern repository-local transient outputs that are admitted before execution, may exist during a command, must be cleaned, and must be absent before the terminal receipt?

problem_statement.root_cause: The public Task Session contract has no distinct transient-output partition. governance-run request declared_outputs are durable staged postimages; executor receipt outputs must resolve to present regular exact-byte artifacts; reconcile maps those durable outputs positionally to material targets. WP-RMT-002 instead declares seven Cargo target directories that may exist only during execution and must be absent before its terminal receipt.
problem_statement.contradiction: A Cargo target directory cannot simultaneously be a present regular exactArtifactRef required by executor receipt reconciliation and an absent-at-closeout transient output.
problem_statement.why_not_mechanical: Changing only the WP-RMT-002 terminal validator or fast-entry terminal-only executionOutputs comparison would either misclassify a transient directory as a durable staged postimage, omit a real write from admission, or fabricate cleanup evidence. The repair changes the public request, ticket, admission, executor evidence, reconciliation, and skill semantics.

invariants: every repository write is admitted before the first write
durable staged postimages remain exact regular artifacts and retain one-to-one material-target reconciliation
transient paths are explicitly admitted, repository-contained, collision-checked, and disjoint from material and durable staged outputs
executor evidence proves whether each transient was touched and whether cleanup completed
every transient is absent before the terminal receipt is written
the terminal receipt remains the final write
no DomainSpec-private vocabulary or semantics enter public Arcanum contracts

decision_dimensions.choice_required: Whether to add an optional typed transient_outputs partition to governance request and execution ticket, and its exact closed row schema.
Whether mutation-admission executionOutputs denotes durable staged outputs, transient outputs, closeout terminal output, or their complete union, and how internal run evidence is excluded.
The canonical touched and cleanup evidence that is verifiable after the transient path has been removed without treating the removed directory as an exactArtifactRef.
Where transient cleanup is checked relative to executor receipt, durable postimage reconciliation, commit, and the final Task Session receipt.
Whether the additive contract remains v1-compatible or requires versioned request, ticket, executor-receipt, and mutation-admission schemas.

options.label: First-class transient partition
options.summary: Add a public, optional typed transient_outputs partition across request, ticket, admission projection, executor receipt evidence, and reconciliation while preserving declared_outputs for durable staged postimages.
options.benefit: Represents the actual lifecycle directly, retains material-only baselines, and can prove both bounded use and absence before terminal receipt.
options.cost_risk: Requires an owner-approved public schema/version decision, migration rules, generated package parity, and a new cleanup-evidence protocol.
options.downstream_impact: Task Session SKILL 37a/37g/48a; mutation admission request/receipt and verifier; governance request/ticket/executor schemas; runner; regression harness; generated Codex and Claude packages; WP-RMT-002 proposal regeneration.

options.label: Executor-owned scratch profile
options.summary: Move transient directories into a Task Session-owned isolated scratch root and exclude them from the Work Pack repository write partition, binding only the scratch-root lifecycle receipt.
options.benefit: Avoids mixing transient directories with durable postimage reconciliation.
options.cost_risk: Changes the seven Work Pack command and write-scope semantics, requires a generic scratch-root authority contract, and may weaken exact repository write accounting if under-specified.
options.downstream_impact: Public executor sandbox contract plus fresh Work Pack planning, readiness audit, and exact-byte acceptance.

options.label: Durable Cargo output
options.summary: Retain each Cargo target directory as a durable declared output and inventory it as reconciliation material.
options.benefit: Fits the current present-output model with fewer schema concepts.
options.cost_risk: Contradicts the accepted cleanup-before-receipt semantics, creates large unstable build artifacts, and changes product evidence boundaries.
options.downstream_impact: Reauthor all seven SWUs and repeat product-semantic owner acceptance; unsuitable without an explicit semantics reversal.

recommendation.rationale: It preserves the accepted material and cleanup semantics and makes the missing lifecycle explicit. The owner must still choose the exact public row, admission-union, evidence, sequencing, and versioning contract before any candidate is authored.

minimum_regression_matrix: non-transient material-bound plan-once execution remains byte-compatible
declared durable staged postimages still map one-to-one to material targets
declared transient directory may be created, used, cleaned, and proven absent before terminal receipt
missing transient declaration blocks before executor launch
extra or substituted transient path blocks before executor launch
path escape, symlink, and overlap with material or durable outputs block
missing or false cleanup evidence blocks
forged cleanup evidence with a live transient path blocks
transient residue blocks before executor and Task Session terminal receipts
durable output incorrectly labeled transient blocks
admission union omission or inflation blocks
Cargo coverage passes for exactly seven WP-RMT-002 units and fails on missing or substituted paths
canonical and generated runner/schema packages remain exact parity
next_action: The public Task Session API owner selects and specifies one option; Invoke then authors a new isolated candidate with canonical tests and generated parity for fresh independent validation and exact-byte owner acceptance.
